seoTitle: Zakynthos cruise port guide: tender, town and Navagio
seoDescription: Most ships tender into Zante Town harbour; Solomos Square is 5 min on foot. Bochali castle €4 (2026). Navagio beach landings banned to 31 Oct 2026.
quickAnswer: Most cruise ships anchor off Zakynthos Town and tender passengers into the main harbour, which is also the ferry port; some cruise line pages say ships may dock, so check your daily programme. Solomos Square is about five minutes' walk from the drop-off, so you need no transport for the town. Be back at the tender pier 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Zakynthos Town is the island's capital and main ferry port, rebuilt after the 1953 earthquake on a flat strip between the harbour and the Bochali hill. There is no dedicated cruise terminal: ships usually anchor in the bay and tenders land you on the town waterfront. The town itself is easy on foot. The famous sights, Navagio (Shipwreck Beach) and the Blue Caves, are on the far north and west coasts, and in 2026 the Navagio beach and bay are closed to landing and swimming, so plan around viewing it from a boat offshore.
tenderNotes: There is no dedicated cruise berth. Most ships anchor in the bay outside Zakynthos Town and run tenders to the main harbour in the town centre, which also serves the island's ferries. Celebrity's port page mentions both docking and tendering, and MSC says the ship may anchor offshore, so confirm on board which applies to your call. MSC notes that tenders may not suit guests with reduced mobility or balance problems. Tender tickets may be issued on board in the morning; Royal Caribbean guests collected them before going ashore in 2022.

terminals.name: Zakynthos Town harbour (tender landing)
terminals.notes: Tenders land on the town waterfront in the main harbour, which is also the ferry port. Solomos Square is about a five-minute walk. No dedicated cruise terminal building. A car rental agency operates at the port and taxis are plentiful.

walkability.detail: Zakynthos Town is flat and compact. Solomos Square is about five minutes from the tender drop-off and St Mark's Square and Alexandrou Roma street are just behind it. The only climb is to Bochali and the Venetian castle: a 20–30 minute walk on a steep, well-marked path, or a short taxi ride.

transportSections.detail: Walk along the waterfront (Strata Marina) from the tender landing to Solomos Square. The whole town centre, including St Dionysios church, is walkable.

transportSections.time: 10–15 min to Tsilivi or Kalamaki; 30–40 min to the Vasilikos beaches
transportSections.detail: Taxis are plentiful near the port and many drivers speak English. Agree the fare before you set off, and arrange a fixed pick-up time for the return.

transportSections.cost: Check fares at the KTEL station
transportSections.detail: The KTEL bus station is in Zakynthos Town. Buses run to Laganas, Kalamaki, Argassi, Tsilivi, Alykes and the Vasilikos beaches, several times a day on weekdays and Saturdays and less often on Sundays. Summer timetables change often, so confirm times at the station (phone +30 26950 22255). Tell the driver your stop, as minor stops can be skipped. With few return buses, this is a poor choice on a tender day.

transportSections.time: 40–50 min to Porto Vromi or the Navagio viewpoint area
transportSections.detail: A rental agency is at the port. Traffic and parking are difficult in peak season. Quads and mopeds are hired widely but suit only confident riders.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the tender pier 90 minutes before all-aboard: 16:00 for a 17:30 all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: Everyone returns at once in the last two hours and tenders fill slowly. If you go to a beach or the west coast by taxi or car, allow extra time for summer traffic back into town. Boat trips from Zakynthos Town to Navagio take 6–8 hours, which leaves no margin on most calls.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Taxis are the quickest way back from Tsilivi, Kalamaki or Bochali. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Walk the town free; Bochali castle €4 (2026); taxi to Bochali about €10–12 each way (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Shorter boat trips leave from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos on the far side of the island; long day boats from Zakynthos Town take 6–8 hours
diyVsExcursion.saving: Ship tour often the safer choice

excursionAdvice: Skip the ship tour for Zakynthos Town and Bochali: the town starts at the tender landing and the castle is a short taxi or a steep walk away. The ship's tour earns its price for Navagio and the Blue Caves. The short boat trips start from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos, a 40–50 minute drive or more across the island, and the trips from town take most of a day, so on a tender call the ship's guaranteed return removes real risk. Beach time at Tsilivi or Kalamaki is easy to do yourself by taxi.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship anchors at 08:00, first tenders ashore by about 08:30, a 17:30 all-aboard and a summer day.

steps.what: Tender ashore. Walk along the waterfront to Solomos Square, about five minutes.
Byzantine Museum on Solomos Square (opens 08:00, closed Mondays), before the tour groups arrive.
Taxi up to Bochali, or walk 20–30 minutes if it is cool. Visit the Venetian castle (closes 14:30) and the free viewpoint.
Back down to St Mark's Square: Solomos Museum (09:00–14:00), then the Catholic church of St Mark.
Lunch at a taverna on or near Alexandrou Roma street.
Walk south along the waterfront to the church of St Dionysios. Cover shoulders and knees.
Option: a short taxi to Tsilivi or Kalamaki for a swim, returning to town by 15:30. Otherwise café and shopping on Alexandrou Roma.
Buy mandolato or pasteli at a waterfront kiosk on the way back to the pier.
Join the tender queue, 90 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Solomos Square and the waterfront
sights.why: The town's largest square, named after the poet Dionysios Solomos, with his statue, arcades and the harbour on one side.
sights.tip: The waterfront road, Strata Marina, closes to traffic from early evening in summer; on a cruise day enjoy it in the morning before 11:00.

sights.name: Byzantine Museum
sights.why: Post-Byzantine icons and church art rescued from the 1953 earthquake, in a building on Solomos Square.
sights.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 08:00–16:00. A good shaded stop.

sights.name: Bochali and the Venetian castle
sights.why: The hill above the town, with the walls of the Venetian fortress (completed 1646) and wide views over the harbour.
sights.tip: Castle open 08:00–14:30; hours may vary outside summer. The walk is 20–30 minutes on a steep path; a taxi is about €10–12 each way.

sights.name: Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians
sights.why: Museum on St Mark's Square with the tombs of the poets Dionysios Solomos, who wrote the Greek national anthem, and Andreas Kalvos.
sights.tip: Open daily 09:00–14:00, so go before lunch.

sights.name: Church of St Dionysios
sights.why: Built in 1926, it holds the relics of the island's patron saint.
sights.cost: Free; a small donation or candle is customary
sights.tip: Active place of worship: cover shoulders and knees.

sights.name: St Mark's Square and Alexandrou Roma
sights.why: A smaller, shadier square behind Solomos Square that opens onto the town's main arcaded shopping street.
sights.tip: Many shops close in the afternoon, roughly 14:00–17:30.

sights.name: Navagio (Shipwreck Beach) from the sea
sights.why: The island's best-known view: a wreck on a white cove under high cliffs on the west coast, reached only by boat.
sights.timeNeeded: Half a day or more including the drive
sights.tip: To 31 October 2026, landing and swimming in the cove are banned and boats must stay at least 50 m from the shore. You see it from the water only.

sights.name: Blue Caves
sights.why: Sea caves on the northern tip near Cape Skinari, entered by small boat.
sights.timeNeeded: Half a day including the drive
sights.tip: Boats leave from Agios Nikolaos in the far north, far from the tender pier. On most calls a ship's tour is the safer way to go.

beaches.name: Tsilivi
beaches.howToGetThere: Taxi, or KTEL bus from the town bus station
beaches.note: Organised sandy beach with sunbeds and restaurants, on the coast north of town.

beaches.name: Kalamaki
beaches.note: Organised beach with sunbeds and restaurants. Some Zakynthos beaches are protected turtle nesting areas, so follow posted rules.

beaches.name: Vasilikos peninsula (Banana Beach, Porto Zoro, Porto Roma, Gerakas)
beaches.note: Allow 2–4 hours in total, which suits only a long call.

food.dish: Mandolato (almond nougat) and pasteli (sesame and honey bars)
food.where: Kiosks along Strata Marina, the town waterfront
Tavernas on and around Alexandrou Roma street
Bakeries in the streets behind Solomos Square

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting to step onto Navagio beach or swim in the cove.
commonMistakes.fix: To 31 October 2026 the beach and its waters are closed; boats stay 50 m offshore. Book a trip that views it from the sea, and check the rules for later dates.

commonMistakes.mistake: Booking a full-day boat from Zakynthos Town to Navagio.
commonMistakes.fix: These run 6–8 hours. On a cruise call choose the ship's tour or a short trip from the west or north coast with a fixed return.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving Bochali castle or the museums until the afternoon.
commonMistakes.fix: The castle closes at 14:30, the Solomos Museum at 14:00. Do them in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Returning to the tender pier 30 minutes before all-aboard.
commonMistakes.fix: Aim for 90 minutes before. The return queue builds sharply in the last two hours.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on a KTEL bus to get back from a beach.
commonMistakes.fix: Returns are infrequent and timetables change often. Use a taxi with an agreed pick-up time.

safety: Zakynthos Town is a normal, busy Greek port town and safe for visitors. The real risks are heat on the unshaded Bochali climb, traffic on the waterfront road, and hired quads and mopeds on unfamiliar roads; leave those to confident riders. At Navagio, the 2026 rules ban landing and swimming because of rockfall risk, and police can fine people who break them. Keep an eye on bags on crowded boats and in the busiest streets.
accessibility: The waterfront and the town centre are flat, which makes Solomos Square, St Mark's Square and the main streets manageable for most visitors. Tendering is the main obstacle: MSC warns that tenders may not suit people with disabilities, reduced mobility or balance problems, so ask the ship whether wheelchair users can transfer on the day. Bochali is reached by a steep path; take a taxi instead. Boat trips to the caves and Navagio use small boats that are hard to board.
rainyDay: Spend the day in town: the Byzantine Museum on Solomos Square, the Solomos Museum on St Mark's Square and the church of St Dionysios, with long café stops under the arcades on Alexandrou Roma. Small-boat trips to Navagio and the Blue Caves depend on sea conditions, so have a town plan ready.
crowdTips: Cruise passengers fill the waterfront and squares in the morning; Solomos Square and the museums are quietest before 11:00. Go up to Bochali early, before the heat and the coach groups. Check the schedule for your date: in October 2026, for example, the published calls were single ships (Seabourn Quest, Oceania Insignia and AIDAblu) on separate days.

faqs.a: Usually. Most ships anchor in the bay and tender passengers into the main harbour in Zakynthos Town. Some cruise line pages say ships may dock, so check your daily programme.

faqs.q: Is Zakynthos Town walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. Solomos Square is about five minutes' walk from the tender drop-off, and the centre is flat.

faqs.q: Can you visit Navagio Shipwreck Beach from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Only from the sea in 2026. Landing and swimming are banned to 31 October 2026 and boats must stay 50 m offshore. Short boat trips leave from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos, which are far from the port, so a ship's tour is usually the safer choice.

faqs.q: What can I do in Zakynthos in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Solomos Square, the Byzantine Museum, Bochali and its Venetian castle, the Solomos Museum and St Dionysios church, with a swim at Tsilivi or Kalamaki on a long call.
Tsilivi and Kalamaki are 10–15 minutes by taxi. The Vasilikos beaches, such as Banana Beach and Porto Zoro, are 30–40 minutes away.

faqs.q: How much is Bochali castle in Zakynthos?
faqs.a: €4 per adult in 2026, open 08:00–14:30. The viewpoint is free. A taxi from the waterfront is about €10–12 each way.

faqs.q: Is there a cruise passenger fee in Zakynthos?
faqs.a: Yes. Since July 2025 Greece charges a per-passenger cruise fee; at ports other than Mykonos and Santorini it is €5 in peak season (June–September). It is collected through the ship's agent or cruise line, not paid ashore.
Yes. Take care in the heat, on the roads if you hire a quad or moped, and respect the Navagio closure.
